subject: Civil Engineering
title: Bridge Inspection and Monitoring
description: A quick win: understand Bridge Inspection and Monitoring.

hook.text: Bridge inspectors rappel down cables, crawl inside box girders, and dive underwater.

buildup.text: Visual inspection every two years is the minimum. Critical bridges get annual checks.

discovery.text: Sensors now monitor strain, vibration, and temperature in real time — digital twins.

twist.text: Drones can inspect bridge undersides in hours — work that once took days with cranes.

climax.text: Structural health monitoring caught a cracked girder on the San Francisco Bay Bridge.

punchline.text: Finding a crack before it spreads saves bridges and lives.

quiz.question: How often must U.S. bridges be visually inspected at minimum?

details.summary: Bridge inspection involves regular visual examination and instrumental assessment of all structural components to detect deterioration before it becomes dangerous.
details.whyItMatters: Routine inspection is the primary defense against bridge failure. Data from inspections drives the allocation of billions of dollars in annual maintenance and replacement funding nationwide.
takeaways: US federal law requires inspection of all public bridges every two years
Inspectors assign condition ratings from 0 to 9 for each component
Structural health monitoring systems provide continuous real-time data

faq.question: What does a bridge inspector look for during routine inspection?
faq.answer: Inspectors examine concrete for cracking, spalling, and rebar exposure; steel for corrosion, fatigue cracks, and section loss; bearings for seized or displaced conditions; expansion joints for damage; and foundations for scour or settlement.

faq.question: How do structural health monitoring systems work on bridges?
faq.answer: Sensors including strain gauges, accelerometers, tilt meters, and GPS receivers are installed at critical locations. They continuously transmit data on stress, vibration, movement, and deformation.
